summary: A 1956 steel tower on the Tonto National Forest's highest Sierra Ancha summit, where writer Edward Abbey once worked two seasons as the lookout.

facts.design: Steel tower, flat roof steel 14' x 14' CL-100 cab, ~41 ft tower height

access.note: Reached by Forest Road 487, which is gated about 0.5 mi short of the trailhead near the tower; the adjoining Sierra Ancha Wilderness is closed to motorized travel.

visit.trail_note: Abbey's Way Trail #151 approaches the lookout area; FR 487 closed ~1/2 mile before the trailhead

events.note: Earlier wooden D-6 cupola groundhouse on the site
Current steel tower with flat-roof CL-100 cab erected, replacing the 1925 wooden lookout
Registered November 27, 1996 as US 192, AZ 2, nominated by District Ranger James R. Soeth

evidence.supports: 1956 steel tower replaced 1925 wooden D-6 cupola groundhouse
evidence.quote: Aztec Peak Lookout was erected in 1956 on the Pleasant Valley Ranger District of the Tonto National Forest. It replaced a wooden D-6 cupola groundhouse built in 1925. It is a steel tower with flat roof steel 14’ x 14’ CL-100 cab. The lookout continues in active service.

evidence.supports: Aztec Peak is the highest point of the Sierra Ancha, in rough/dissected terrain near the Mogollon Rim
evidence.quote: Aztec Peak forms the highest point of the Sierra Ancha, an elevated and deeply dissected mountain region between the Tonto Basin and the Mogollon Rim.
An earlier lookout house was constructed during the 1920s, while the present steel tower dates to 1956 . The tower rises approximately 41 feet and supports a steel lookout cab.

evidence.supports: elevation 7,728 ft / 2,355 m; on Tonto National Forest

evidence.quote: Edward Abbey (1927-1989) an environmental writer, worked for two seasons as a lookout at Aztec Peak and made reference to it in his writing.

evidence.supports: Forest Road 487 gated about half a mile before the trailhead; high clearance recommended on upper route
evidence.quote: The Forest Service’s Abbey’s Way information notes that FR 487 is closed approximately half a mile before the trailhead near the lookout area. Road closures, wildfire impacts, fallen trees, snow, erosion, and seasonal weather can all change access. Visitors should check current Tonto National Forest conditions before traveling. Even when roads are open, a high-clearance vehicle may be appropriate for the upper portions of the route.

evidence.supports: Sierra Ancha Wilderness closed to motorized travel, borders the lookout's road access
evidence.quote: This distinction matters for visitors because motorized and mechanized travel is prohibited within designated wilderness even though roads approach the Aztec Peak summit area.

evidence.supports: trail toward tower named for Abbey; near end of FR 487 near lookout tower
evidence.quote: East end: Near the end of Forest Road (FR) 487, a short distance from Aztec Peak lookout Tower.

notes_for_editor: The FS trail page lists the trail under the Payson Ranger District; the NHLR page (and the record) say Pleasant Valley Ranger District. Both are districts of Tonto National Forest; this may reflect a later district reorganization rather than a factual error, but I did not resolve it and left the record's district attribution untouched. Height (~41 ft) and the 'closed to motorized travel' wilderness note come from Mountain Field Guide, a secondary aggregator that cites the Forest Service and Peakbagger; treat with slightly less confidence than the NHLR and USFS primary sources. Climbability of the tower itself (public access to the cab) is not established by any source read; left as unknown.
